svg.title: Where bonobos live
svg.desc: A simplified diagram of the Congo Basin in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Bonobos live only south of the Congo River, which runs north out of the south east of the country, curves west along the equator and then turns south west to the Atlantic. Marked are Kokolopori, run by the Bongandu people, the Lola ya Bonobo sanctuary near Kinshasa, and Ekolo ya Bonobo, the forest where rescued bonobos are released. At least 15,000 to 20,000 are thought to survive.
